blindSpots: A shared-work group evaluation does not exercise member-hostname branches on all four physical machines.
Evaluation and derivation forcing do not prove activation, runtime health, or successful host deployment.
Flake schemas and bounded custom probes force only declared normal forms; arbitrary lazy values outside those contracts remain unknown.
Nix evaluating-file diagnostics prove only that file evaluation started, not that parsing completed or lazy contents were forced.
No portable mandatory shell line-coverage backend exists in the locked environment; static lint evidence is not behavioral evidence.
No raw option values, environments, credentials, activation scripts, or service configuration may be persisted in a coverage artifact.
Pre-commit has a hard 120-second envelope including its five-second kill grace; expensive consumes the CI/on-demand ceiling, while pre-push remains a selector and planning ceiling.
Python inventory assignment and linting are not dynamic line or branch coverage; subprocess and alternate-interpreter execution require explicit coverage.py handling.
The internal-json diagnostic wording is not a stable coverage API; parser drift must produce unknown or failure, never an empty passing numerator.
VPS, Vulcan, and shared-work consumer evidence depends on local or LAN consumer roots and is not GitHub-hosted CI evidence.
config/ai/flake.nix is an intentional throwing stub verified by immutable-subflake-check's negative probe; successful Nix evaluation cannot positively reach it.
readFile, readDir, hashFile, pathExists, copied paths, and some scoped imports are invisible to file-reach diagnostics.
An evaluation-start event precedes parse and evaluation success.
Lazy expressions and non-evaluation file reads are not observed.
Directory events from scopedImport are not credited as default.nix.
